binding_force.rationale: The General Policy for the Safe and Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems (1 April 2025) is an MTCIT policy without statutory force; no AI bill is before a legislature.

implementation.rationale: The 2025 General Policy is adopted with MTCIT and sector regulators named for oversight, but no implementing regulations, standards or deadlines have been issued.

scope.rationale: The 2025 General Policy binds public entities and addresses relevant private actors as guidance, with no sector-specific binding AI duties anywhere.

academia.rationale: Universities contributed to National AI Policy 2025 consultations and host the AI Centres of Excellence, without a formal standing advisory seat.

civil_society.rationale: Digital Rights Foundation's May 2026 analysis records limited and non-transparent consultation on the National AI Policy 2025, with no standing civil society role.

industry.rationale: Industry was consulted on the National AI Policy 2025, and the Islamabad AI Declaration 2026 frames a private sector-led, government-enabled model presented at the Indus AI Summit 2026.

international.rationale: Pakistan adopted its own Islamabad AI Declaration in February 2026 and pursues bilateral AI cooperation, without binding treaty or standards-body commitments.

actions_taken.rationale: Enforcement involving AI-generated content proceeds under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016; no decision under any AI-specific rule exists.

dedicated_authority.rationale: The Pakistan Digital Authority was directed in February 2026 to operationalise a national AI Supervisory Framework but has no dedicated AI enforcement resources or rules.

monitoring_practice.rationale: Audits, a public registry of automated systems and a National Data Maturity Index are proposed in the National Data Governance Policy 2026 and not yet operating.

sanctions_framework.rationale: No penalties attach to AI-specific obligations; only Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 offences, including the 2025 section 26A, reach AI-related conduct.

formal_coordination.rationale: Coordination runs through the National Digital Commission and the AI Council under the National AI Policy 2025, with a National Data Governance Council only proposed.

nongovernmental_checks.rationale: Courts and independent bodies have no established role in AI oversight; review of automated decisions exists only as a proposed right in the National Data Governance Policy 2026.

regulator_plurality.rationale: Pakistan Digital Authority leads AI governance alongside sectoral regulators, including the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority and the State Bank of Pakistan.

subnational_role.rationale: Provinces are represented in the AI Council and proposed data governance structures but adopt no AI regulation of their own.

binding_instruments.rationale: Only general law applies to AI: Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 (amended 2025) and the Digital Nation Pakistan Act 2025, neither containing AI-specific obligations.

economic_tools.rationale: National AI Fund, Ignite-financed AI programmes and AI Centres of Excellence operate under the National AI Policy 2025; the State Bank of Pakistan sandbox is financial, not AI-specific.

institutional_capacity.rationale: Pakistan Digital Authority, created by the Digital Nation Pakistan Act 2025 and named national AI governance body, has issued no AI rules and exercised no compliance powers.

soft_law.rationale: National AI Policy 2025, Islamabad AI Declaration 2026 and National Data Governance Policy 2026 set published guidance including generative-AI and automated-decision controls for public bodies.

implementation.rationale: National AI Policy 2025 (cabinet-approved July 2025) has no implementing rules; the AI Supervisory Framework the Prime Minister directed PDA to operationalise in February 2026 is not issued.

scope.rationale: AI-specific obligations exist only for federal public bodies under the non-binding National Data Governance Policy 2026; private-sector AI use is uncovered.

academia.rationale: Palauan researcher Joleen Ngoriakl advocates Pacific perspectives in global AI safety debate, with no domestic advisory role in government AI policy.

civil_society.rationale: No AI consultation or advisory process includes Palauan non-governmental organisations.

industry.rationale: No consultation, working group or standing forum gives Palauan business a role in AI policy.

international.rationale: Palau is associated with the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence as a member state but has signed no AI-specific declaration, treaty or standards process.

actions_taken.rationale: No enforcement action concerning AI has been taken; responses to deepfakes targeting President Whipps in May 2026 were public warnings by officials and media.

dedicated_authority.rationale: No authority owns AI enforcement; the Office of Applied Technology and Strategy and the Bureau of Cybersecurity have cybersecurity and IT remits only.

monitoring_practice.rationale: No AI audit, inspection or monitoring programme exists; planned monitoring under the Cybersecurity Act covers government network security.

sanctions_framework.rationale: Only general-law penalties could reach AI conduct, such as the civil penalties of up to $10,000 for misuse of protected data in the Cybersecurity Act (2026).

nongovernmental_checks.rationale: No Palauan court ruling, ombudsman finding or independent review has addressed AI systems.

regulator_plurality.rationale: No body holds an AI remit; technology authority is concentrated in the presidential Office of Applied Technology and Strategy and the new Bureau of Cybersecurity.

soft_law.rationale: No national AI principles, ethics document, guidance or standard has been published by any Palauan ministry or office.

ai_specificity.rationale: Only general law touches AI incidentally; no Palauan regulator or court has applied privacy, consumer or cybersecurity law to an AI system.

implementation.rationale: No AI instrument exists to implement, and no competent authority for AI has been designated.

scope.rationale: No sector or use case is covered by AI rules; the Cybersecurity Act 2026 and Privacy Act (Title 6, Palau National Code) contain no AI provision.

formal_coordination.rationale: With no AI mandate assigned to any body, no interagency AI coordination mechanism exists.

nongovernmental_checks.rationale: No Tuvaluan court judgment, ombudsman inquiry or independent review has addressed AI systems.

regulator_plurality.rationale: No body regulates AI; the Department of ICT within the responsible ministry is the single actor in digital policy.

subnational_role.rationale: Island kaupule councils have no role in digital or AI regulation, which sits entirely with central government.

binding_instruments.rationale: No binding AI instrument exists, and the Tuvalu Telecommunications Corporation Act 2008 and related regulations contain no AI provisions.

economic_tools.rationale: No AI funding scheme, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule exists; digital spending is directed to the Tuvalu Vaka submarine cable and broadband rollout.

institutional_capacity.rationale: The Department of ICT and Tuvalu Telecommunications Corporation hold no AI mandate, and no AI unit, council or office has been created.

soft_law.rationale: No national AI guidance, ethics principles, standard or code has been published by any Tuvaluan ministry.

ai_specificity.rationale: The Tuvalu National ICT Policy (approved 5 October 2023) addresses connectivity, digital government and cybersecurity without AI provisions, and no general law carries AI-specific text.

binding_force.rationale: No AI-specific binding rule exists or is before Parliament; the AI Asia Pacific Institute's 2024 Pacific survey records Tuvalu as having no AI strategy or policy.

implementation.rationale: No AI instrument has been adopted, so no implementing rules, guidance or competent authority exist.

scope.rationale: No sector, use case or public-sector AI deployment is covered by any Tuvaluan rule written for AI.

civil_society.rationale: Civil society organisations including CIPESA took part in the UNESCO RAM consultations and published AI policy recommendations, without any standing formal role.

industry.rationale: Private-sector participants joined the UNESCO AI RAM workshops of 19 February and 26 May 2026 and the National AI and Emerging Technologies Strategy consultations.

international.rationale: Uganda runs the UNESCO AI RAM process, used ITU support for its National AI Landscape Assessment, works with UNDP, and aligns with the African Union Continental AI Strategy.

binding_instruments.rationale: Only general statutes reach AI: the Data Protection and Privacy Act No. 9 of 2019 and the Computer Misuse Act (Cap. 96).

scope.rationale: No binding AI rule covers any sector; the only instrument in effect is the non-binding Código de Ética published by MINCYT on 19 February 2026.

academia.rationale: Academic and research institutes contributed to drafting and to the UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment, without a statutory standing advisory body.

civil_society.rationale: Independent NGOs have no standing role; input channels run through state-linked associations and general consultation on draft legislation.

industry.rationale: The draft AI Law was released for public consultation in September 2025 and industry coalitions filed submissions on the implementing decree in May 2026.

international.rationale: Vietnam hosted the Sixth ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting that adopted the Hanoi Digital Declaration (January 2026), participates in ASEAN AI work and the 2026 China-ASEAN AI roundtable.

actions_taken.rationale: No enforcement decision under the AI Law has been published; compliance grace periods run to March and September 2027.

dedicated_authority.rationale: The Ministry of Science and Technology is the designated AI authority for the whole regime but has not published use of inspection or sanctioning powers.

monitoring_practice.rationale: Decree 142/2026/ND-CP requires risk-classification notification and serious-incident reporting to the Ministry of Science and Technology through the national AI portal, with no public monitoring…

sanctions_framework.rationale: Article 29 of Law 134/2025/QH15 provides for administrative, civil and criminal liability plus suspension and recall, while the decree setting AI fine levels has not been issued.

formal_coordination.rationale: A National Committee on Artificial Intelligence chaired by the Prime Minister with the Ministry of Science and Technology as standing body sits above ministry-level coordination.

nongovernmental_checks.rationale: Review of AI decisions runs through general administrative complaint and court channels; no independent AI oversight body or AI case law exists.

regulator_plurality.rationale: State administration of AI is centralized in the Ministry of Science and Technology, with sectoral ministries and the State Bank issuing only complementary technical guidance.

subnational_role.rationale: Vietnam is a unitary state; provincial People's Committees carry out local administrative tasks and no province regulates AI.

binding_instruments.rationale: Law 134/2025/QH15, Decree 142/2026/ND-CP and Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg are in force, with their principal obligations still inside transition periods.

economic_tools.rationale: Decree 142/2026/ND-CP establishes a controlled AI sandbox with approval procedures alongside Decree 353/2025/ND-CP digital-technology sandbox and National AI Strategy funding, with no AI procurement…

institutional_capacity.rationale: The Ministry of Science and Technology holds the statutory AI mandate and runs the national AI portal, with no sandbox approvals, conformity decisions or inspections published.

soft_law.rationale: Circular No. 05/2026/TT-BKHCN issued the National AI Ethics Framework, building on Decision No. 1290/QD-BKHCN (2024) guidelines for responsible AI research and development.

ai_specificity.rationale: Law No. 134/2025/QH15 is a dedicated horizontal statute on AI systems, supplemented by Decree 142/2026/ND-CP and Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg.

binding_force.rationale: Law No. 134/2025/QH15 on Artificial Intelligence in force since 1 March 2026, but main compliance duties are subject to grace periods to March and September 2027.

implementation.rationale: Framework is in a transition period: Decree 142/2026/ND-CP and Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg apply, while the administrative-sanctions decree is pending and general compliance deadlines run to 2027.

scope.rationale: The AI Law and Decree 142/2026/ND-CP cover all providers, developers, deployers and users across sectors, while high-risk duties under Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg phase in through 2027.

academia.rationale: Yemeni universities publish AI research but hold no advisory role in government AI policy.

civil_society.rationale: Domestic NGOs have no role in any AI policy process; Yemeni participation in the UN Special Envoy's AI and Women, Peace and Security workshop at the Paris AI Action Summit in February 2025 was…

industry.rationale: No consultation, working group or formal channel exists for telecom operators or technology firms to feed into AI policy.

international.rationale: Yemen attended the REAIM Summit in Seoul on 9-10 September 2024 with a Deputy Foreign Minister-led delegation but has not signed an AI declaration or joined standards work.

actions_taken.rationale: No AI-related enforcement action, investigation or decision by any Yemeni authority has been recorded.

dedicated_authority.rationale: No authority in Aden or Sana'a owns AI enforcement.

monitoring_practice.rationale: No audit, inspection or monitoring program covers AI systems in Yemen.

sanctions_framework.rationale: No penalty attaches to any AI-specific obligation because no such obligation exists in Yemeni law.

formal_coordination.rationale: No interagency AI coordination mechanism, committee or working group exists in Yemen.

nongovernmental_checks.rationale: No Yemeni court ruling, ombudsman decision or independent review concerning AI has been recorded.

regulator_plurality.rationale: No body holds an AI remit; the duplicated Ministry of Telecommunications and Information Technology reflects conflict fragmentation rather than plural AI regulators.

subnational_role.rationale: Governorates and local authorities have issued no AI rules and play no role in AI oversight.

binding_instruments.rationale: No binding instrument of any kind addresses AI; Yemen also lacks a comprehensive data protection statute that regulators could apply to AI.

economic_tools.rationale: No AI funding program, procurement rule or regulatory sandbox exists; activity is limited to occasional public-sector AI training courses such as the April 2026 course on AI in administrative and…

institutional_capacity.rationale: No AI unit, council or agency exists; the Ministry of Telecommunications and Information Technology operates in two parallel forms under Aden and Sana'a.

soft_law.rationale: No national AI ethics principles, guidance, codes or standards have been issued by either administration.

ai_specificity.rationale: Only general law (1994 Penal Code, telecommunications rules) touches AI incidentally; the draft law on information technology crimes remains unenacted and contains no AI provision.

binding_force.rationale: Neither the Aden government nor the Sana'a authority has enacted or tabled any binding AI rule; no AI bill exists in any legislative process.

implementation.rationale: No AI instrument exists to implement, and no competent authority for AI has been designated.

scope.rationale: No sector, use case or content type is covered by AI-specific rules in Yemen.

academia.rationale: Academic and research institutions contributed to the national strategy and attended the June 2026 UNESCO Readiness Assessment Methodology consultation.

civil_society.rationale: Civil society, youth organisations and media were among participants in the AI Readiness Assessment Methodology 2.0 consultation convened in Lusaka on 22-23 June 2026.

industry.rationale: Private sector actors took part in the strategy's stakeholder consultations and in the Ministry-UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment Methodology 2.0 expert consultation of 22-23 June 2026.

international.rationale: Zambia aligns its strategy with the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, the African Union Continental AI Strategy and OECD AI Principles, and piloted UNESCO RAM 2.0 as the first Southern…

actions_taken.rationale: No AI-specific obligation exists in Zambian law and no enforcement decision concerning AI systems has been recorded by any Zambian authority.

dedicated_authority.rationale: ZICTA, the Zambia Cyber Security Agency and the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner act within existing remits; none holds an AI mandate.

monitoring_practice.rationale: Monitoring consists of the strategy's monitoring and evaluation framework and the one-off UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment conducted in 2026.

sanctions_framework.rationale: Penalties reaching AI-related conduct exist only in general law, notably the Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025 and the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021.

formal_coordination.rationale: Coordination rests on the National AI Council and technical working groups set out in the 2024 strategy, with cooperation so far occurring through ad hoc ministry-convened workshops.

nongovernmental_checks.rationale: No Zambian court ruling, ombudsman decision or independent review body has addressed AI governance.

regulator_plurality.rationale: The Ministry of Technology and Science leads AI policy while ZICTA, the Smart Zambia Institute and the Data Protection Commissioner operate without any AI remit.

subnational_role.rationale: Zambia is a unitary state and no province or local authority holds any role in AI policy or implementation.

binding_instruments.rationale: Only general law reaches AI: Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021, Cyber Security Act No. 3 of 2025 and Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025.

economic_tools.rationale: The strategy announces an Emerging Technologies Centre of Excellence and AI innovation support, with no disbursed AI funding programme, AI procurement rules or operating regulatory sandbox.

institutional_capacity.rationale: The National AI Council and technical working groups are advisory structures provided for in the strategy, with no legal AI mandate conferred by statute.

soft_law.rationale: The National Artificial Intelligence Strategy is a single high-level document setting ethical principles aligned to the UNESCO Recommendation and OECD AI Principles, with no codes or standards issued.

ai_specificity.rationale: Only general law touches AI incidentally: Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021, Cyber Security Act No. 3 of 2025 and Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025.

binding_force.rationale: The National Artificial Intelligence Strategy launched by the Ministry of Technology and Science in 2024 calls for a future National AI Policy and regulation, with no AI bill before Parliament.

implementation.rationale: Zambia's only AI instrument is the non-binding National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, a paper commitment with no implementing rules or designated competent authority.

scope.rationale: No binding rule written for AI covers any sector; the Cyber Security Act No. 3 of 2025 and Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025 contain no AI-specific obligations.

academia.rationale: Academia contributed to the multi-stakeholder drafting process and the strategy designates AI Centres of Excellence at leading universities.

civil_society.rationale: Civil society organisations were among stakeholders consulted during strategy drafting, and MISA Zimbabwe publishes rights-based critiques of the AI governance architecture.

industry.rationale: Private sector actors took part in the consultative workshops in Kadoma, Harare, Bulawayo and Masvingo that produced the strategy, without standing formal roles.

international.rationale: The strategy was informed by UNESCO's AI Readiness Assessment Methodology and launched with the UN Resident Coordinator; Zimbabwe engages African Union and SADC AI initiatives.

actions_taken.rationale: POTRAZ began mandatory data-protection inspections of data controllers on 1 September 2026 under general law; no AI-specific enforcement decision exists.

dedicated_authority.rationale: POTRAZ enforces within its existing data protection and telecommunications remit; the AI Strategy Implementation Office holds no enforcement powers.

monitoring_practice.rationale: AI monitoring is confined to the strategy's planned reporting by the AI Strategy Implementation Office and the UNESCO readiness assessment as a one-off study.

sanctions_framework.rationale: Penalties reaching AI arise only from the Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] (2021), including offences for processing personal data without a licence.

formal_coordination.rationale: The strategy creates a National Digital Regulatory Committee chaired by the President with the Ministry as secretariat and a Steering Committee housed in POTRAZ, bodies not yet operational.

nongovernmental_checks.rationale: The proposed AI Ethics Board and parliamentary standing committee are not constituted, and no Zimbabwean court or ombudsman decision on AI exists.

regulator_plurality.rationale: The Ministry of Information Communication Technology, Postal and Courier Services leads AI policy, with POTRAZ the only regulator holding any related statutory remit.

subnational_role.rationale: Provinces and local authorities hold no AI regulatory role; the strategy's Community AI Councils are awareness structures, not regulators.

binding_instruments.rationale: Only general law binds — the Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] (2021) and the 2024 Licensing of Data Controllers Regulations.

economic_tools.rationale: The Mugove/Umqele/Isabelo co-investment fund, Project Pangolin data platform and the Innovation Crucible regulatory sandbox are announced in the strategy and not yet operating.

institutional_capacity.rationale: The National AI Council, AI Strategy Implementation Office and Technical Working Groups are strategy-created coordination bodies with no statutory AI mandate.

soft_law.rationale: The National AI Strategy 2026–2030 sets Ubuntu-grounded ethical principles; no AI standards or codes have been issued by Standards Association of Zimbabwe or POTRAZ.

ai_specificity.rationale: AI is governed through the general Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] (2021), which contains no provision written for AI systems.

binding_force.rationale: National AI Strategy 2026–2030, launched 13 March 2026, commits to enacting a National AI Act with a risk-based approach, which remains undrafted and not before Parliament.

implementation.rationale: The strategy was adopted by Cabinet in October 2025 and launched in March 2026 with no implementing rules, AI guidance or competent AI authority operational.

scope.rationale: No binding AI instrument covers any sector; the only AI document is the non-binding National AI Strategy 2026–2030.
